subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend five properties we can test in materials, with one quick home test for each.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko paanch properties samjhao jo hum materials mein test kar sakte hain, aur har ek ka ghar pe karne wala ek chhota test.
answer: Key ideas: lustre (look for shine); hardness (press or scratch gently with a fingernail); transparency (hold it up to a light); solubility (stir a little into water); floating or sinking (put it in a bucket of water).

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what do we call a material that lets some light through, but we can't see clearly through it?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jo material thodi roshni jaane deta hai par usme se saaf nahi dikhta, use kya kehte hain?
answer: Translucent.

subject: science
prompt_en: Group these materials into transparent and opaque: glass, wood, clear plastic sheet, iron, cardboard.
prompt_hi: In materials ko transparent aur opaque mein baanto: kaanch, lakdi, saaf plastic sheet, loha, gatta.
answer: Transparent: glass, clear plastic sheet. Opaque: wood, iron, cardboard.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict (don't touch to check!): after cooking, which part of a frying pan will be hot, the metal pan or its plastic handle? Why?
prompt_hi: Guess karo (chhoo ke check mat karna!): khaana banane ke baad kadhai ka kaunsa hissa garam hoga, dhaatu wala ya plastic ka handle? Kyon?
answer: The metal pan is hot; the plastic handle stays fairly cool, because heat does not pass through plastic easily.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if a raincoat were made of cotton cloth instead of plastic, what would happen in the rain?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar raincoat plastic ki jagah cotton ke kapde ka hota, toh baarish mein kya hota?
answer: Water would soak through the cotton and you would get wet; plastic is waterproof, so it keeps water out.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the handle stays cool. Then why is the pan itself made of metal and not plastic?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha handle thanda rehta hai. Toh kadhai khud dhaatu ki kyon hoti hai, plastic ki kyon nahi?
answer: Heat passes through metal quickly to cook the food, and metal doesn't melt on the stove; plastic would melt or burn and passes heat poorly.

subject: science
prompt_en: A steel spoon and a wooden spoon are the same object made of different materials. Name one property where they differ and one job each is better for.
prompt_hi: Steel ki chammach aur lakdi ki chammach, object ek hi hai par material alag. Ek property batao jisme farak hai, aur ek kaam jiske liye har ek behtar hai.
answer: For example: heat passes through steel easily (it gets hot in hot dal) but not through wood; wood is better for stirring hot food in a pan, steel is better for eating and easy to clean. Steel is shiny and wood is dull.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are school benches usually made of wood or metal, and never of glass?
prompt_hi: School ki bench aam taur pe lakdi ya dhaatu ki kyon hoti hai, kaanch ki kabhi kyon nahi?
answer: Wood and metal are strong and don't break easily; glass breaks easily and the sharp pieces would be dangerous.

subject: science
prompt_en: You are choosing a water bottle for a school trip where it might get dropped. Which material would you choose, and why?
prompt_hi: School trip ke liye paani ki botal chun rahe ho, jahan woh gir sakti hai. Kaunsa material chunoge, aur kyon?
answer: Steel or strong food-safe plastic, because they don't break when dropped and don't leak; glass would break.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a Venn diagram with two circles, 'Shiny' and 'Floats on water'. Place a steel spoon, a wooden block, a shiny plastic ball and a stone.
prompt_hi: Do gol ghero wala Venn diagram banao, 'Chamakdaar' aur 'Paani pe tairta hai'. Usme steel ki chammach, lakdi ka block, chamakdaar plastic ki ball aur patthar rakho.
answer: Shiny only: steel spoon. Floats only: wooden block. Both: shiny plastic ball. Outside both: stone.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu's list of 'materials' is: chair, wood, bottle, plastic, spoon, steel. What is wrong with his list?
prompt_hi: Golu ki 'materials' ki list hai: kursi, lakdi, botal, plastic, chammach, steel. Uski list mein kya galat hai?
answer: Chair, bottle and spoon are objects, not materials; the materials in his list are wood, plastic and steel.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain why a pressure cooker's body is metal but its handles are plastic, using the words material, property and use.
prompt_hi: Samjhao ki pressure cooker ka body dhaatu ka aur handle plastic ke kyon hote hain, 'material', 'property' aur 'use' shabd use karke.
answer: Key ideas: the body's material is metal, whose property is that heat passes through it quickly and it doesn't melt, so its use is cooking food; the handles' material is plastic, whose property is that heat doesn't pass through it easily, so its use is safe holding.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: is steel an object or a material? Name two objects made from it.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: steel object hai ya material? Usse bani do cheezein batao.
answer: A material; e.g. a spoon, tumbler, almirah or plate.

subject: science
prompt_en: What do we use to measure temperature, and in what unit?
prompt_hi: Temperature naapne ke liye kya use karte hain, aur kis unit mein?
answer: A thermometer; degrees Celsius (°C).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: keep your left hand in cold water and your right hand in comfortably warm water (never hot!) for a minute, then put both hands into the same lukewarm water. How will it feel to each hand?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: left haath thande paani mein aur right haath halke garam paani mein (garam bilkul nahi!) ek minute rakho, phir dono ek hi gungune paani mein daalo. Har haath ko kaisa lagega?
answer: The left (cold) hand will feel the lukewarm water as warm; the right (warm) hand will feel it as cool, even though it is the same water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: on a winter morning you touch a steel almirah handle and a wooden door at the same time. Which feels colder? Are they at different temperatures?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: sardi ki subah tum ek saath steel ki almari ka handle aur lakdi ka darwaza chhoote ho. Kaun zyada thanda lagega? Kya dono ka temperature alag hai?
answer: The steel feels colder, but both are at the same room temperature; metal takes heat from your hand faster.

subject: science
prompt_en: Think it through (this one is only a thought experiment, don't try it with hot water): which can melt more ice cubes in total before it cools down, one spoonful of hot water or a whole bucket of warm water?
prompt_hi: Sirf socho (ye sirf sochne wala experiment hai, garam paani se try mat karna): thanda hone se pehle kaun zyada barf ke tukde pighla sakta hai, ek chammach garam paani ya poori baalti gunguna paani?
answer: The bucket of warm water: it is at a lower temperature, but there is so much more water that it holds much more heat.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the steel and the wood are at the same temperature. Why does the steel feel colder, then?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha steel aur lakdi ka temperature same hai. Toh steel zyada thanda kyon lagta hai?
answer: Metal takes heat away from our hand much faster than wood does, so our hand cools faster and the metal feels colder.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a cup of hot chai and a bucket of warm bathwater. Which has the higher temperature? Which holds more heat?
prompt_hi: Garam chai ka cup aur nahaane ke gungune paani ki baalti compare karo. Kiska temperature zyada hai? Kisme zyada heat hai?
answer: The chai has the higher temperature; the bucket holds more heat because there is far more water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your little brother says the floor tiles are 'colder' than the carpet in the same room. What would you tell him?
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota bhai kehta hai ki ek hi kamre mein tiles carpet se zyada 'thande' hain. Tum use kya bataoge?
answer: Both are at the same room temperature; the tiles take heat from his feet faster, so they feel colder.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do we wear woollen sweaters in winter? Do sweaters make heat?
prompt_hi: Sardi mein hum woollen sweater kyon pehente hain? Kya sweater garmi banata hai?
answer: No, wool doesn't make heat; it traps air and slows heat leaving our body, so we stay warm.

subject: science
prompt_en: Place these on a Celsius number line: ice melting (0 °C), normal body temperature (about 37 °C), water boiling (100 °C), a hot summer afternoon in Delhi (about 45 °C).
prompt_hi: In sab ko Celsius number line pe lagao: barf pighalna (0 °C), shareer ka saamaanya temperature (lagbhag 37 °C), paani ubalna (100 °C), Delhi ki garmi ki dopahar (lagbhag 45 °C).
answer: In order: 0 °C (ice melting), 37 °C (body), 45 °C (Delhi summer), 100 °C (boiling water).

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Heat and temperature are the same. A big bucket of warm water has a higher temperature than a small cup of hot chai, because it has more heat.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Heat aur temperature ek hi hain. Gungune paani ki badi baalti ka temperature garam chai ke chhote cup se zyada hai, kyonki usme zyada heat hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Temperature measures how hot something is, and the chai is hotter; the amount of heat also depends on how much water there is. Heat and temperature are different.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child why we use a thermometer instead of our hand, using the three-bowl experiment.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko 3 katori wale experiment se samjhao ki hum haath ki jagah thermometer kyon use karte hain.
answer: Key ideas: a hand from cold water feels lukewarm water as warm, and a hand from warm water feels the same water as cool; so touch depends on the hand and is unreliable (and unsafe for very hot things); a thermometer gives the same number in °C for everyone.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: at what temperature does pure water freeze, in °C?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: shuddh paani kis temperature pe jamta hai, °C mein?

subject: science
prompt_en: On a lab thermometer there are 10 small divisions between the 20 °C and 30 °C marks. What does each small division stand for?
prompt_hi: Lab thermometer pe 20 °C aur 30 °C ke beech 10 chhote khaane hain. Har chhota khaana kitne ka hai?

subject: science
prompt_en: On a clinical thermometer there are 10 small divisions between 37 °C and 38 °C. The reading is 4 small divisions after 37. What is the temperature?
prompt_hi: Clinical thermometer pe 37 °C aur 38 °C ke beech 10 chhote khaane hain. Reading 37 ke baad 4 khaane aage hai. Temperature kitna hai?

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you take a lab thermometer out of warm water and wait 30 seconds before reading it. Will the reading be the same as it was in the water?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: lab thermometer ko garam paani se nikaal ke 30 second baad padho. Kya reading wahi hogi jo paani mein thi?
answer: No; once out of the water it starts changing towards room temperature (it falls if the water was warmer than the room).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: can a clinical thermometer show the temperature of cold water from the fridge (about 5 °C)?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: kya clinical thermometer fridge ke thande paani (lagbhag 5 °C) ka temperature dikha sakta hai?
answer: No; its scale starts at about 35 °C, so it can't show 5 °C. Use a lab thermometer.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said to read the lab thermometer while it's still in the water. Why?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha lab thermometer ko paani ke andar rehte hue hi padho. Kyon?
answer: Once it's out, it starts gaining or losing heat to the air and the reading changes, giving a wrong value.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer: range, use and one special feature.
prompt_hi: Clinical aur laboratory thermometer compare karo: range, use aur ek khaas baat.
answer: Clinical: about 35-42 °C, for body temperature; a mercury one has a kink so the reading stays until shaken, and digital ones beep when done. Lab: about −10 to 110 °C, for liquids and experiments; no kink, so it must be read while in the liquid.

subject: science
prompt_en: A digital thermometer shows 101.3 °F for your sister. Normal is about 98.6 °F. Does she have a fever?
prompt_hi: Digital thermometer tumhari behen ka 101.3 °F dikhata hai. Normal lagbhag 98.6 °F hai. Kya use bukhaar hai?
answer: Yes; it is about 2.7 °F above normal (about 38.5 °C), which is a fever, so tell an adult.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your science-fair team wants to record how fast hot water cools in a steel tumbler and in a clay kulhad (a teacher or other adult pours the hot water). Which thermometer will you use, and what are two rules for reading it correctly?
prompt_hi: Tumhari science fair team record karna chahti hai ki garam paani steel ke tumbler aur mitti ke kulhad mein kitni jaldi thanda hota hai (garam paani teacher ya koi bada hi daalega). Kaunsa thermometer use karoge, aur sahi padhne ke do niyam batao.
answer: A laboratory thermometer (an adult pours the hot water). Rules (any two): keep the bulb in the water without touching the bottom or sides; keep it upright; read while it's still in the water; keep your eye level with the top of the column.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a lab thermometer scale from 20 °C to 40 °C with a mark at every 1 °C. Shade the liquid up to 33 °C. How many small divisions above 30 °C did you shade?
prompt_hi: 20 °C se 40 °C tak lab thermometer ka scale banao, har 1 °C pe nishaan. 33 °C tak liquid ko rang do. 30 °C ke upar kitne chhote khaane rangeen kiye?
answer: 3 divisions above 30 °C.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu wants to check if the chai is too hot by dipping the family's clinical thermometer in it. What is the problem, and what should be used instead?
prompt_hi: Golu ghar ke clinical thermometer ko chai mein daal ke dekhna chahta hai ki chai zyada garam hai ya nahi. Dikkat kya hai, aur iski jagah kya use karna chahiye?
answer: Chai is far above 42 °C, so a clinical thermometer can't measure it and may break (mercury ones release poisonous mercury); a lab thermometer should be used, with an adult's help.

subject: science
prompt_en: Teach your cousin how to take someone's temperature correctly with a clinical thermometer, with an adult helping.
prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko sikhao ki clinical thermometer se kisi ka temperature sahi kaise lete hain, kisi bade ki madad se.
answer: Key ideas: an adult helps; a digital thermometer is safest for children; clean it; for a mercury type, an adult shakes it until it reads below 35 °C; place it in the armpit (for children, armpit is safer than the mouth, since a glass one can break); wait the full time (a few minutes in the armpit, or until a digital one beeps); read it holding it at eye level; clean it again; normal is about 37 °C (an armpit reading is a little lower).

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is normal human body temperature in °C?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: insaan ke shareer ka saamaanya temperature °C mein kitna hota hai?
answer: About 37 °C.

subject: science
prompt_en: What do we call (a) ice turning into water, (b) water turning into ice, (c) water vapour turning into water?
prompt_hi: Inhe kya kehte hain: (a) barf ka paani banna, (b) paani ka barf banna, (c) bhaap ka paani banna?
answer: (a) Melting, (b) freezing, (c) condensation.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you pour a glass of water into a flat plate, then from the plate into a tall bottle. Does the amount of water change? Does its shape change?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek glass paani ko pehle chapti plate mein daalo, phir plate se lambi botal mein. Kya paani ki matra badlegi? Kya uska aakaar badlega?
answer: The shape changes to fit each container, but the amount (volume) of water stays the same.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: an ice cube in a glass and a spoon of sugar stirred into a glass of water both 'disappear'. Is it the same kind of change?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: glass mein rakha ice cube aur paani mein ghuli ek chammach cheeni, dono 'gayab' ho jaate hain. Kya dono ek hi tarah ka badlaav hai?
answer: No. The ice melts: a solid becomes a liquid because of warmth, and it is still water. The sugar dissolves: it spreads into the water to form a sugar solution; it hasn't melted.
